question: With what heavenly blessings has God the Father blessed believers in Christ according to Ephesians 1:3?
opt1: Blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ
opt2: Endowed us with material riches and earthly political domains
opt3: Promised us exemption from mortal death and physical pain on earth
opt4: Granted us authority to govern secular Roman municipalities
correct: Blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ
explanation: God the Father has lavished upon believers every spiritual blessing originating from and located in the heavenly realm in Christ. Ephesians 1:3 (KJV) - "Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ:"

question: When did God choose believers in Christ, and for what moral purpose in Ephesians 1:4?
opt1: Chosen us when we first performed legal works under the Mosaic law
opt2: Chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love
opt3: Selected us after evaluating our natural philosophical achievements
opt4: Ordained us when we arrived at the assembly of the saints in Ephesus
correct: Chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love
explanation: Sovereign election occurred in eternity past prior to creation, aiming at our ultimate personal holiness and blamelessness in divine love. Ephesians 1:4 (KJV) - "According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love:"

question: Unto what status did God predestinate believers according to the good pleasure of His will in Ephesians 1:5?
opt1: Unto perpetual servitude under guardian tutors in the temple
opt2: Unto biological supremacy over all pagan Gentile nations
opt3: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself
opt4: Unto temporal dominion over the merchant trade of Asia Minor
correct: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself
explanation: Believers are predestined to full familial adoption as God's beloved children through Jesus Christ according to His gracious will. Ephesians 1:5 (KJV) - "Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will,"

question: What redemptive blessing do believers possess in Christ through His sacrificial blood in Ephesians 1:7?
opt1: A certificate of exemption from paying provincial taxes to Caesar
opt2: A written guarantee of earthly affluence and physical longevity
opt3: Temporal immunity from legal interrogation before municipal magistrates
opt4: In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace
correct: In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace
explanation: Full redemption and complete pardon for sins are purchased by the blood of Christ and bestowed according to the inexhaustible riches of grace. Ephesians 1:7 (KJV) - "In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace;"

question: What grand cosmic purpose in the dispensation of the fulness of times did God make known in Ephesians 1:9-10?
opt1: That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth
opt2: That the Roman empire might conquer all eastern kingdoms under Christian banners
opt3: That the ceremonial sacrifices of the Jerusalem temple might be instituted globally
opt4: That all material creation might be dissolved into an ethereal void without form
correct: That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth
explanation: God's eternal mystery unites and consummates all things in the universe under the sovereign headship of Jesus Christ. Ephesians 1:10 (KJV) - "That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven, and which are on earth; even in him:"

question: According to what sovereign counsel does God work all things in granting believers an inheritance in Ephesians 1:11?
opt1: According to the fluctuating desires and petitions of mortal kings
opt2: According to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will
opt3: In response to the astrological courses of the planetary heavens
opt4: Through negotiations conducted between angels and human philosophers
correct: According to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will
explanation: God's sovereign providence executes everything in total conformity with His eternal, unthwartable, and self-determined purpose. Ephesians 1:11 (KJV) - "In whom also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will:"

question: With what divine seal and guarantee were believers sealed after trusting in the gospel of salvation in Ephesians 1:13-14?
opt1: With an imperial signet ring stamped by the governor of Asia
opt2: With an engraved tablet of bronze deposited in the municipal hall
opt3: Ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, which is the earnest of our inheritance
opt4: With a parchment certificate authorized by the elders of Antioch
correct: Ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, which is the earnest of our inheritance
explanation: The Holy Spirit indwells believers as God's personal seal of ownership and the pledge (earnest) guaranteeing their final inheritance. Ephesians 1:13-14 (KJV) - "In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, unto the praise of his glory."

question: What spiritual illumination did Paul pray the Father of glory would grant the Ephesians in Ephesians 1:17-18?
opt1: The ability to master secular Greek poetry and public rhetoric
opt2: A vision revealing the exact date of the destruction of the world
opt3: Supernatural insight to discover hidden veins of gold in the mountains
opt4: The spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him: the eyes of your understanding being enlightened
correct: The spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him: the eyes of your understanding being enlightened
explanation: Paul petitioned God to grant inward spiritual illumination so they might fully comprehend the hope of His calling and His riches. Ephesians 1:17-18 (KJV) - "That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him: The eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that ye may know what is the hope of his calling, and what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints,"

question: Where did God the Father seat Christ after raising Him from the dead by His mighty power in Ephesians 1:20?
opt1: Set him at his own right hand in the heavenly places
opt2: Placed him upon the royal throne of David in earthly Jerusalem
opt3: Stationed him as commander over the legions of imperial Rome
opt4: Established him as chief high priest within the earthly sanctuary
correct: Set him at his own right hand in the heavenly places
explanation: Christ was exalted to supreme sovereign authority at the Father's right hand in the heavenly realm above all created powers. Ephesians 1:20 (KJV) - "Which he wrought in Christ, when he raised him from the dead, and set him at his own right hand in the heavenly places,"

question: How does Paul describe the church in relation to Christ in Ephesians 1:22-23?
opt1: A temporal guild of religious artisans maintaining sacred customs
opt2: Gave him to be the head over all things to the church, which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all
opt3: A regional council subordinate to the municipal senate of Ephesus
opt4: An academic society investigating the moral laws of nature
correct: Gave him to be the head over all things to the church, which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all
explanation: Christ is the supreme Head of the church, which is His spiritual body, embodying the vital fulness of Him who fills all in all. Ephesians 1:22-23 (KJV) - "And hath put all things under his feet, and gave him to be the head over all things to the church, Which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all."

question: What was the former spiritual condition of believers before being quickened by God in Ephesians 2:1?
opt1: Who were merely morally sick and seeking philosophical medicine
opt2: Who were innocent children uncorrupted by societal traditions
opt3: Who were dead in trespasses and sins
opt4: Who were righteous scholars striving to keep the ceremonial law
correct: Who were dead in trespasses and sins
explanation: Apart from divine grace, unregenerate humanity is spiritually dead: entirely devoid of spiritual life and alienated from God. Ephesians 2:1 (KJV) - "And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins;"

question: How does Paul designate the demonic ruler governing the course of this fallen world in Ephesians 2:2?
opt1: The emperor sitting upon the imperial throne of Rome
opt2: The angel of the bottomless pit named Apollyon in Hebrew
opt3: The secular governor presiding over the province of Asia
opt4: The prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience
correct: The prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience
explanation: Satan exercises malevolent spiritual influence over the atmosphere of this fallen world, energizing rebellious unbelievers. Ephesians 2:2 (KJV) - "Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience:"

question: What motivated God to quicken believers together with Christ even when they were dead in sins in Ephesians 2:4-5?
opt1: God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us
opt2: The impressive moral purity and righteousness demonstrated by mankind
opt3: The animal sacrifices offered daily upon the temple altars
opt4: The intellectual wisdom displayed by ancient Greek philosophers
correct: God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us
explanation: Regeneration originates solely in God's abundant compassions and profound eternal love, completely independent of human merit. Ephesians 2:4-5 (KJV) - "But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us, Even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ, (by grace ye are saved;)"

question: Where has God exalted and seated believers together with Christ in Ephesians 2:6?
opt1: In the physical court of the Sanhedrin on Mount Moriah
opt2: Hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus
opt3: Upon the judgment benches of the Roman provincial tribunals
opt4: In the ancestral palaces of the kings of Judah
correct: Hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus
explanation: By virtue of vital union with Christ, believers share in His resurrection, ascension, and heavenly enthronement. Ephesians 2:6 (KJV) - "And hath raised us up together, and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus:"

question: How is salvation received according to the famous declaration in Ephesians 2:8-9?
opt1: By ceremonial compliance with the legal washings and circumcision of Moses
opt2: Through personal moral virtue achieved by philosophical discipline
opt3: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: not of works, lest any man should boast
opt4: By performing extraordinary acts of penance and charitable almsgiving
correct: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: not of works, lest any man should boast
explanation: Salvation is entirely an unearned gift of divine grace apprehended through faith, completely excluding all human boasting. Ephesians 2:8-9 (KJV) - "For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast."

question: What are believers declared to be, and for what purpose were they created in Christ Jesus in Ephesians 2:10?
opt1: We are autonomous beings created to pursue our own pleasure and worldly ambitions
opt2: We are servants bound under the legal curse of the Mosaic ordinances
opt3: We are mortal accidents of nature destined to perish without eternal purpose
opt4: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them
correct: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them
explanation: Believers are God's masterwork (poiema), re-created in Christ not by good works, but for the fruitful practice of pre-ordained good works. Ephesians 2:10 (KJV) - "For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them."

question: How were Gentile believers formerly described before coming to Christ in Ephesians 2:12?
opt1: Aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world
opt2: Equally possessors of the prophetic scriptures and temple priesthood
opt3: Full participants in the patriarchal promises made to Abraham
opt4: Enlightened seekers who possessed saving knowledge of the Almighty
correct: Aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world
explanation: Gentiles were historically excluded from Israel's covenant privileges, living in tragic spiritual destitution without God and without hope. Ephesians 2:12 (KJV) - "That at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world:"

question: How have those who were once far off been brought near, and what did Christ break down in Ephesians 2:13-14?
opt1: Made nigh by submitting to the ceremonial rite of physical circumcision

opt3: Brought near through the philosophical treaties negotiated in Athens
opt4: Unified by imperial decree enforcing Roman citizenship upon all nations
correct: Made nigh by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us
explanation: The blood of Christ reconciles Gentiles, demolishing the dividing barrier (the ceremonial law) that separated Jews and Gentiles. Ephesians 2:13-14 (KJV) - "But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ. For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us;"

question: What did Christ create out of the two formerly divided groups (Jews and Gentiles) in Ephesians 2:15?
opt1: A confederation of independent national congregations
opt2: A dual covenant system recognizing two separate ways of salvation
opt3: To make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace
opt4: A legal court to adjudicate ceremonial disputes between tribes
correct: To make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace
explanation: Christ created a completely unprecedented entity: the church, 'one new man', reconciled in one body through the cross. Ephesians 2:15 (KJV) - "Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances; for to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace;"

question: Upon what foundation is the household of God built, and who is the chief corner stone in Ephesians 2:20?
opt1: Built upon the philosophical doctrines of Socrates and Plato

opt4: Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone
correct: Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone
explanation: The church rests immovably upon apostolic and prophetic revelation, with Jesus Christ Himself as the foundational, unifying cornerstone. Ephesians 2:20 (KJV) - "And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone;"

question: How does Paul identify himself at the beginning of Chapter 3 regarding his imprisonment?
opt1: I Paul, the prisoner of Jesus Christ for you Gentiles

explanation: Paul viewed his Roman incarceration not as a defeat by Caesar, but as a sovereign captivity for the sake of the Gentile mission. Ephesians 3:1 (KJV) - "For this cause I Paul, the prisoner of Jesus Christ for you Gentiles,"

opt1: That all pagan temples must be converted into Jewish synagogues

correct: That the Gentiles should be fellowheirs, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the gospel
explanation: The mystery is the full, equal inclusion of Gentiles with Jews in one body, sharing identically in the gospel promise in Christ. Ephesians 3:6 (KJV) - "That the Gentiles should be fellowheirs, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the gospel:"

question: With what humble self-appraisal does Paul describe his apostolic commissioning in Ephesians 3:8?

explanation: Deeply conscious of his former persecution of the church, Paul considered himself the least of all saints, marveling at grace. Ephesians 3:8 (KJV) - "Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ;"

question: To whom was the manifold wisdom of God to be made known through the church according to Ephesians 3:10?

explanation: The church serves as God's cosmic showcase, displaying His multi-faceted wisdom to angelic hierarchies in heavenly realms. Ephesians 3:10 (KJV) - "To the intent that now unto the principalities and powers in heavenly places might be known by the church the manifold wisdom of God,"

question: What confident privilege do believers enjoy through faith in Jesus Christ in Ephesians 3:12?

opt4: We receive secret knowledge hidden from ordinary human beings

explanation: Christ grants believers unrestricted, confident, and joyful access into the holy presence of God without fear of rejection. Ephesians 3:12 (KJV) - "In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him."

question: Before whom does Paul bow his knees in prayer for the Ephesian believers in Ephesians 3:14-15?

explanation: Paul bows in reverent prayer before God the Father, the sovereign Creator and Patriarch of the entire redeemed family. Ephesians 3:14-15 (KJV) - "For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, Of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named,"

question: What internal spiritual strengthening does Paul petition for the believers in Ephesians 3:16?

question: Where does Paul pray that Christ may dwell, and how in Ephesians 3:17?

explanation: Paul yearned for Christ to make His permanent, settled home in their hearts through faith, anchoring them deeply in love. Ephesians 3:17 (KJV) - "That Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love,"

question: What fourfold dimensions of Christ's love are believers to comprehend with all saints in Ephesians 3:18-19?

question: What majestic doxology crowns the conclusion of Paul's prayer in Ephesians 3:20-21?

Amen."

question: How does the apostle Paul urge believers to walk regarding their calling in Ephesians 4:1-2?

question: What sevenfold unity of the Christian faith is enumerated in Ephesians 4:4-6?

question: What did Christ do when He ascended up on high according to the quote from Psalm 68 in Ephesians 4:8?
opt1: When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men

opt1: To collect imperial taxes and enforce civic obedience to Rome

question: From what instability does spiritual maturity preserve believers according to Ephesians 4:14?
opt1: From experiencing physical aging, bodily sickness, and mortality

explanation: Doctrinal maturity prevents believers from being gullible and swept away by cunning deceptive heresies and false teachings. question: How does the body of Christ grow and edify itself according to Ephesians 4:15-16?
opt1: Speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ

opt4: Conforming the gospel message to the popular culture of Ephesus

question: What transformation of the mind and nature is commanded in Ephesians 4:22-24?
opt1: Modify external manners while retaining the corrupt inward nature

explanation: True sanctification involves stripping off the old corrupt nature, mental renewal by the Spirit, and putting on the new creation. question: What rule concerning anger and the adversary is articulated in Ephesians 4:26-27?

explanation: Unresolved anger gives Satan an immediate operational foothold (foothold/place) to fracture fellowship and foster bitterness. Ephesians 4:26-27 (KJV) - "Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath: Neither give place to the devil."

question: Why must believers avoid corrupt communication and bitterness according to Ephesians 4:30?
opt1: Lest the Roman guards overhear and report our speeches to Caesar
opt2: Lest our commercial merchant contracts in Ephesus be canceled
opt3: Lest our social status among the Greek philosophers be tarnished
opt4: And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption
correct: And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption
explanation: Sinful speech and interpersonal malice bring profound sorrow to the indwelling Holy Spirit who seals believers unto final glory. Ephesians 4:30 (KJV) - "And grieve not the holy Spirit of God, whereby ye are sealed unto the day of redemption."

question: Whom are believers commanded to imitate as dear children, walking in love in Ephesians 5:1-2?
opt1: Be ye therefore followers of God, as dear children; and walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us
opt2: Imitate the powerful kings and conquerors who subjugated the nations
opt3: Follow the philosophical sages who debated in the academies of Athens
opt4: Imitate the ceremonial rigor of the scribes and priests of the temple
correct: Be ye therefore followers of God, as dear children; and walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us
explanation: Christian ethics is grounded in imitating God's character and walking in self-sacrificial love patterned after Christ's cross. Ephesians 5:1-2 (KJV) - "Be ye therefore followers of God, as dear children; And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour."

question: What idolatrous sin is equated with covetousness in Ephesians 5:5, excluding one from the kingdom of Christ and of God?
opt1: Engaging in honest commercial trade in the public market
opt2: Nor covetous man, who is an idolater, hath any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God
opt3: Investing money in agricultural land and maritime ships
opt4: Receiving wages for lawful manual craftsmanship in Ephesus
correct: Nor covetous man, who is an idolater, hath any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God
explanation: Greed and covetousness dethrone God, making wealth an idol; chronic idolatrous covetousness excludes one from God's kingdom. Ephesians 5:5 (KJV) - "For this ye know, that no whoremonger, nor unclean person, nor covetous man, who is an idolater, hath any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God."

question: How should believers conduct themselves regarding the unfruitful works of darkness in Ephesians 5:11?
opt1: Participate quietly in secret pagan mysteries to gain knowledge
opt2: Compromise with immoral practices to maintain social popularity
opt3: And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them
opt4: Ignore moral evil completely, treating all conduct as morally neutral
correct: And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them
explanation: Believers must refuse all complicity in wicked practices, exposing and reproving them with the light of divine truth. Ephesians 5:11 (KJV) - "And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them."

question: What wake-up call of spiritual resurrection is quoted in Ephesians 5:14?
opt1: Flee into the mountains of Cappadocia before the winter arrives
opt2: Offer forty days of ceremonial prayers before the sacred altar
opt3: Inscribe the ten commandments upon the doorposts of your houses
opt4: Awake thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light
correct: Awake thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light
explanation: Paul summons sleeping believers to shake off spiritual stupor and arise into the radiant illumination of Christ. Ephesians 5:14 (KJV) - "Wherefore he saith, Awake thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light."

question: Why are believers exhorted to walk circumspectly, redeeming the time in Ephesians 5:15-16?
opt1: See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, redeeming the time, because the days are evil
opt2: Because the civil courts of Rome require daily registration of hours
opt3: Because commercial merchants who waste time lose their profit
opt4: Because the stars in their courses predict an imminent famine
correct: See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, redeeming the time, because the days are evil
explanation: Living in an evil and fallen age demands vigilant wisdom, seizing every opportunity to advance God's kingdom purposes. Ephesians 5:15-16 (KJV) - "See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil."

question: What contrast does Paul draw with drunkenness in Ephesians 5:18?
opt1: Drink only imported wines certified by Jewish dietary inspectors
opt2: And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit
opt3: Take strong drink in private while abstaining in public gatherings
opt4: Fast from all food and beverages for forty consecutive days
correct: And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit
explanation: Instead of alcoholic intoxication that leads to reckless debauchery, believers must be continually filled and controlled by the Holy Spirit. Ephesians 5:18 (KJV) - "And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit;"

question: What joyful musical worship results from being filled with the Spirit in Ephesians 5:19?
opt1: Chanting esoteric spells learned from the occult scrolls of Ephesus
opt2: Reciting political elegies in praise of the Roman provincial governor
opt3: Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord
opt4: Engaging in theatrical choral performances for municipal applause
correct: Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord
explanation: The Spirit-filled life overflows in corporate and personal worship, offering heartfelt praise to the Lord through varied spiritual songs. Ephesians 5:19 (KJV) - "Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord;"

question: How are Christian wives exhorted to relate to their husbands in Ephesians 5:22?
opt1: Wives, demand complete financial independence from your households
opt2: Wives, rule over your husbands with strict domestic legislation
opt3: Wives, defer only to civil judges in matters of family authority
opt4: Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord
correct: Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord
explanation: Wives are called to voluntary, loving submission to their husbands as a reflection of the church's devotion to the Lord. Ephesians 5:22 (KJV) - "Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord."

question: What divine standard of love are Christian husbands commanded to demonstrate toward their wives in Ephesians 5:25?
opt1: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it
opt2: Husbands, exercise tyrannical dominance over all household decisions
opt3: Husbands, provide material wealth while withholding personal affection
opt4: Husbands, love your wives only so long as they never disagree with you
correct: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it
explanation: Husbands are called to unconditional, sacrificial, self-giving love modeled after Christ's total sacrifice for His bride, the church. Ephesians 5:25 (KJV) - "Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it;"

question: What profound mystery does the marriage union of one flesh ultimately signify according to Ephesians 5:31-32?
opt1: A temporary civil contract ratified by the municipal magistrate
opt2: This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church
opt3: A commercial alliance between prominent merchant families of Asia
opt4: An allegory illustrating the political pact between Rome and Greece
correct: This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church
explanation: Human marriage is a living parable created by God to picture the sacred, indissoluble covenant between Jesus Christ and His church. Ephesians 5:32 (KJV) - "This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church."

question: What command and promise are given to children regarding their parents in Ephesians 6:1-3?
opt1: Children, depart from your parents upon reaching twelve years of age
opt2: Children, obey only when your parents agree with your personal desires
opt3: Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise
opt4: Children, report all parental discipline to the civic magistrates
correct: Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise
explanation: Filial obedience in the Lord is right and carries God's ancient promise of well-being and longevity upon the earth. Ephesians 6:1-3 (KJV) - "Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise; That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth."

question: How are Christian fathers instructed to raise their children in Ephesians 6:4?
opt1: Exercise severe physical tyranny to crush their youthful spirits
opt2: Permit them complete moral autonomy without any guidance
opt3: Train them exclusively in secular Greek rhetoric and warfare
opt4: Fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord
correct: Fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord
explanation: Fathers must avoid exasperating their children through harshness, nurturing them patiently with the Lord's instruction. Ephesians 6:4 (KJV) - "And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord."

question: How should Christian servants perform their daily labor according to Ephesians 6:5-6?
opt1: Not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart
opt2: Work vigorously only when the overseer is physically present
opt3: Engage in secret sabotage against harsh and unreasonable masters
opt4: Demand immediate legal emancipation before performing any duty
correct: Not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart
explanation: Christian workers are to labor sincerely and conscientiously, viewing their earthly employment as sacred service directly unto Christ. Ephesians 6:6 (KJV) - "Not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart;"

question: What reminder did Paul give Christian masters regarding their treatment of servants in Ephesians 6:9?
opt1: Masters hold absolute authority over servants with no divine accountability
opt2: Knowing that your Master also is in heaven; neither is there respect of persons with him
opt3: Masters may threaten and execute servants without violating Christian love
opt4: Masters are spiritually superior to servants in the kingdom of God
correct: Knowing that your Master also is in heaven; neither is there respect of persons with him
explanation: Masters and servants stand as absolute equals before their heavenly Master, who judges all without partiality. Ephesians 6:9 (KJV) - "And, ye masters, do the same things unto them, forbearing threatening: knowing that your Master also is in heaven; neither is there respect of persons with him."

question: Why must the Christian soldier put on the whole armour of God in Ephesians 6:11?
opt1: To conquer physical territories and overthrow Roman legions
opt2: To achieve prestige and worldly recognition in the agora
opt3: That ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil
opt4: To intimidate secular magistrates during public interrogations
correct: That ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil
explanation: The full divine armor is essential to withstand and defeat the cunning stratagems, deceitful schemes, and ambushes of Satan. Ephesians 6:11 (KJV) - "Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil."

question: Against what enemies does the Christian truly wrestle according to Ephesians 6:12?
opt1: Against political candidates competing in the municipal elections
opt2: Against commercial merchants who compete with our crafts in the marketplace
opt3: Against our biological kin who refuse to accept our theological doctrines
opt4: Not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places
correct: Not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places
explanation: The ultimate conflict is cosmic and supernatural, waged against demonic powers and evil spiritual hierarchies rather than mortal humans. Ephesians 6:12 (KJV) - "For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places."

question: What pieces of armor represent truth, righteousness, and the gospel preparation in Ephesians 6:14-15?
opt1: Your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness; and your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace
opt2: Golden coronets of civic pride, iron gauntlets of wrath, and boots of swift vengeance
opt3: Purple robes of imperial rank, linen phylacteries of the law, and sandals of ascetic pilgrimage
opt4: Bronze shields of ancestral philosophy, spears of human rhetoric, and helmets of academic pride
correct: Your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness; and your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace
explanation: Paul details the Christian's defensive equipment: the belt of truth, breastplate of righteousness, and footwear of gospel readiness. Ephesians 6:14-15 (KJV) - "Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness; And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace;"

question: What offensive and defensive function does the shield of faith serve in Ephesians 6:16?
opt1: It grants physical immunity against imperial Roman swords
opt2: Taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked
opt3: It guarantees that believers will never suffer poverty or distress
opt4: It deflects all civil taxation levied by municipal magistrates
correct: Taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked
explanation: Unshakable trust in God's promises completely extinguishes the flaming arrows of temptation, doubt, and accusation fired by the adversary. Ephesians 6:16 (KJV) - "Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked."

question: What is the single offensive weapon named in the armour of God in Ephesians 6:17?
opt1: The iron lance forged by the smiths of Macedonia
opt2: The philosophical syllogisms taught in the academies of Athens
opt3: And the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God
opt4: The legal charters ratified by the Sanhedrin in Jerusalem
correct: And the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God
explanation: The sole offensive weapon is the Holy Spirit's sword: the spoken and proclaimed Word of God (rhema theou). Ephesians 6:17 (KJV) - "And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God:"

question: Whom did Paul dispatch to Ephesus to comfort their hearts and declare his affairs in Ephesians 6:21-22?
opt1: Erastus the chamberlain of the city of Corinth
opt2: Silas the prophet from the council of Jerusalem
opt3: Apollos the eloquent teacher from Alexandria
opt4: Tychicus, a beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, shall make known to you all things: whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose
correct: Tychicus, a beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, shall make known to you all things: whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose
explanation: Paul entrusted the delivery of this epistle to Tychicus, a dependable and beloved co-laborer, to encourage the Ephesian believers. Ephesians 6:21-22 (KJV) - "But that ye also may know my affairs, and how I do, Tychicus, a beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, shall make known to you all things: Whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose, that ye might know our affairs, and that he might comfort your hearts."
